Note: -   The assay is very sensitive to preanalytical variables (sample storage, transport, time to processing etc). Please correlate clinically and review if required. 

     Interpretation Guidelines:

  • CD8 counts may change up to 30% without any change in clinical status due to biological and method variation. Therefore, trends over time should be monitored rather than change in a specific test result. (Ref: Wallach: Interpretation of laboratory medicine).
  • For monitoring, both CD8% & Absolute CD8 counts should be considered. However, Absolute CD8 counts can show variation as it depends on absolute lymphocyte count (CD45) & total T-cell count (CD3) within a sample which in turn are affected by various infective/inflammatory conditions. While CD8% is considered a stable parameter as it shows minimal biological variation & least dependent on absolute counts within a sample.
  • An unexpected result must be repeated before changing therapy.
  • Very low CD4/8 absolute cell counts and percentages though satisfactorily acquired by the flow cytometer could be associated with cellular degeneration, hence correlation with clinical findings & viral load is advised. If clinically indicated kindly repeat the test with fresh sample.
  • Factors affecting CD4/CD8 counts: Circadian rhythm, age, sex, ethnic origin, stress, effect of drugs, presence of ant lymphocyte antibody, splenectomise, menstrual cycle, smoking, infections, pregnancy, time of collection, delay in analysis, sequential use of different assay and sample
